subject: Term Wardship: Helix multi-year price safeguard request

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Term Wardship: Helix multi-year price safeguard request

Team —

Quick ask for executive clearance on a non-standard term for Helix Therapeutics (strategic healthcare pilot). Helix is asking for a 3-year committed package with the following commercial deviations from our standard MSA: 

- 3-year price lock (no baseline per-unit price increases for the initial three-year term)
- Annual uplift cap capped at 4% compounded at renewal
- Renewal protection clause: at first renewal, customer guaranteed not to face > uplift cap unless material changes to usage profile

Why this matters: Helix is evaluating Redwood for their inference plane across clinical, R&D, and a pilot production workload. Expected committed spend is ~$1.6M ARR if they hit the commit profile (detailed in the attached term sheet). This is a reference win in a regulated vertical and could meaningfully accelerate sales velocity in adjacent healthcare accounts.

Risks / asks: this is outside our baseline guardrails on price guarantees. I need an exec-level signoff (revenue ops + legal + finance OK to proceed) on offering the above as an exception, conditional on the attached term sheet and the following: 

- Minimum 12-month prepaid invoice or 30% upfront commit (finance condition)
- Usage floor at 70% of committed units; below that we require repricing/termination triggers
- Legal to confirm the exact renewal-protection language (first renewal only or perpetual?)

Attached: helix_term_sheet_v3.pdf (commercials) and redline_master_services_agreement.docx (initial legal ask).

Can we get signoff by COB Tues (Aug 1)? Helix procurement is pushing to close the deal before their Q3 planning meeting.

Thanks —

Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Soojin —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions before I can route to Deal Desk / Finance for a formal economics stamp: 

1) Can you confirm the committed spend cadence (monthly ramp by quarter) and the committed token/embedding volumes we expect in year 1 vs year 3? I want to model the unit economics if they sit at 70% versus 100% of the commit.
2) Is the 4% uplift cap requested by the customer or proposed by us? If customer requested, did they propose any trade (longer term, higher upfront)?
3) Do we have a proposed termination trigger or service-level exit if usage drops materially? Marissa

I also recommend we include a contractual right to reprice if aggregate usage across the contract declines >40% for two consecutive billing periods — this protects us while still giving them a predictable headline price.

On the attachments: Lauren — can you quickly sanity-check the redline around the renewal-protection clause? The way it reads today could be interpreted as a multi-renewal lock which is higher risk.

- Marissa

Subject: Re: Term Wardship: Helix multi-year price safeguard request

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the redline and have the following legal observations: 

- The current "price lock" language as written is broad and could be interpreted to prohibit any future price changes tied to material cost deltas (e.g., cloud GPU price spikes). We should narrow to "no contractual per-unit list price increases during the initial 36-month term except for approved pass-throughs tied to materially increased infrastructure costs (as defined)."
- Renewal protection: strongly recommend limiting the guaranteed protection to the first renewal period following the initial term. Extending protection beyond that materially increases our exposure.
- Add a "material adverse usage" clause: if average monthly consumption for two consecutive quarters falls below 60% of the committed baseline, Redwood reserves the right to re-open price discussions and apply a market adjustment.
- Add an audit right and a quarterly usage reconciliation schedule to verify consumption against the commit.

From a contracting perspective, legal can accept a 3-year lock with a 4% uplift cap provided Finance confirms the upfront commit (30% or 12 months prepay) and Deal Desk confirms the usage floor and repricing trigger language. I attached inline redlines to the docx.

-Lauren

Date: 2028-08-01T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: Helix term safeguard (conditional)

Team —

I reviewed Soojin's note, Marissa's modeling questions, and Lauren's redlines. Given Helix's strategic value and the size of the upfront commit, I am comfortable providing conditional executive approval to proceed with the following guardrails: 

1) Approve 3-year price lock with an annual uplift cap of up to 5% (we can offer 4% if Helix provides 30% upfront or 12-month prepay).
2) Renewal protection limited to the first renewal only; legal to insert clear language to this effect and to define approved pass-throughs.
3) Usage floor: contract to require at least 70% of committed monthly consumption averaged over any rolling quarter; if consumption <70% for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may re-open pricing and apply a market adjustment.
4) Finance condition: receive minimum 30% upfront payment at signing or 12 months prepaid.
5) Deal Desk condition: finalize audit right and reconciliation cadence in the SOW.

These conditions should mitigate downside while allowing us to present a compelling, headline-friendly commercial to Helix. Jordan — please coordinate to get the revised docs out and prepare a one-page exec summary for the CFO sign-off.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Alex —

Great to connect earlier. Per our internal review, Redwood is prepared to move forward with a 36-month committed arrangement with the following approved commercial framework (final doc to follow):

- 36-month price lock for core inference unit pricing, subject to narrowly defined pass-through exceptions.
- Annual uplift cap: up to 5% compounded (we can confirm 4% if Helix provides 30% upfront or elects a 12-month prepay).
- Renewal protection is guaranteed for the first renewal only. Subsequent renewals subject to market adjustments.
- Usage floor: average consumption must be >=70% of committed baseline over any rolling quarter; if consumption falls below that for two consecutive quarters, Redwood retains the right to re-open pricing.
- Finance condition: 30% upfront or 12 months prepay at signing.
- Audit & reconciliation: quarterly reconciliations and audit rights to validate consumption.

Next steps:
1) We will circulate a revised term sheet and redlined MSA today (see DocuSign link once ready).
2) Please confirm acceptance of the 30% upfront or 12-month prepay option and whether you prefer the 4% uplift alternative or the default 5% uplift.
3) Once you confirm, Legal and Deal Desk will prepare the final SOW for signature.

Appreciate the partnership — we recognize Helix's timeline and will prioritize the DocuSign envelope.

Best,
